lesson.subtitle: Lesson 5 -- Scheduling the Call
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Ender de Souza Batista | Lesson 5 -- Scheduling the Call
lesson.grammar_point: prepositions of time: at (times), on (days and dates), in (parts of the day, months, years) + next week

listenings.text: Hi Ender, it's Sarah, from Mastercard. Quick message about the global call. It is not on Thursday at nine anymore. The new day is Friday, at ten in the morning, São Paulo time. That is eight in the morning in New York. The invite is in your email. And the next global call is in December, on the first Friday. Thanks, and have a good day!

In the winter, London is three hours ahead of São Paulo. So my calls with Brazil are always in the afternoon. They are usually at two, London time. That is eleven in the morning in São Paulo: good for everybody. I never have calls on Fridays in the afternoon. On Fridays, I work from home, and I finish early.

extra_audio.text: Priya asks: Are you available on Tuesday? Ender checks his calendar. He is busy in the morning. They schedule the call for Wednesday at nine. In Mumbai, it is five thirty in the afternoon. The second call is next week, on Monday at ten.
